name: ch21_diwali_balcony_photo
alt: A housing society notice board shows a photo of last year's best-lit balcony, and this Diwali residents climb ladders to string lights on their own balconies to beat it.
scene: A wide view of an Indian housing society on Diwali evening, the sky still pale but lamps glowing warm. LEFT foreground: a wooden-framed notice board on a pillar near the gate with a single pinned photo of a balcony glowing with fairy lights, a small card under it reading "B-304", and nothing else on the board: no prize poster, no announcement. A woman in her 40s (plum saree) stands looking at it with a thoughtful half-smile, hand on her chin. RIGHT half: a four-storey apartment block with two wings, balconies stacked in rows; most balconies now strung with amber and coral fairy-light dots, diyas on railings and a paper lantern hanging in one. A young man in a teal kurta stands on an aluminium ladder against a second-floor balcony, stretching a light string; a teenage girl on the balcony above leans over holding the other end; an older man on the ground steadies the ladder and points up, directing. Only one top-floor balcony is still dark, showing the change is spreading. A dashed arrow runs from the photo on the notice board to the glowing building, showing the photo started it. Mood: festive, quietly competitive, warm evening light on a pale ground. Label: "BEAT THE PHOTO" across the top centre of the picture.

key: Two neighbouring tea stalls at a railway station
name: ch21_tea_stalls_best_chai
alt: Two railway tea stalls: on the left the owners scowl in a price war with falling signs, on the right both proudly serve the best masala chai to happy commuters.
scene: A split-panel picture divided by a thin vertical line, the same two side-by-side tea stalls on an Indian railway platform in both halves, with a yellow platform edge, a pillar and a station clock behind. Each stall is a small wooden cart with a steel kettle on a stove, glass tumblers and a stack of rusks. Owner one is a man in his 50s with a grey moustache and an amber vest; owner two is a younger man in a teal shirt with a towel on his shoulder. LEFT panel: the owners glare at each other with folded arms, each stall has a price card, one reading "Rs 9" and the other "Rs 8", a big coral downward arrow between them, a near-empty cash tin with one coin and a red cross badge; a single commuter shrugs. RIGHT panel: the same two men each hold up a steaming tumbler of masala chai with pride, small cardamom and ginger icons over their kettles, gold stars above each stall, and two commuters (a woman office worker with a laptop bag and an older man with a newspaper) sip happily with green ticks beside them. Morning platform light, cheerful on the right and tense on the left. Labels: "PRICE WAR" at the top of the left panel, "BEST CHAI" at the top of the right panel.

key: best batsman pulls out of the final
name: ch21_captain_jab_pads_up
alt: In a college cricket dressing room, the captain teases the out-of-form star batsman about scoring 90 in the semis, and the batsman starts strapping on his pads.
scene: Inside a small college cricket dressing room: wooden benches, kit bags, a rack of bats, a whiteboard and a window showing the green ground and a white sight screen outside. CENTRE-LEFT: the team's star batsman, a lanky 20-year-old in cricket whites, sits on the bench, head slightly down, with his pads lying beside him, but in this moment he is already reaching for one pad and buckling it onto his shin, a small determined frown forming. RIGHT: the captain, also in whites with a teal team cap, stands with one hand on his hip and the other pointing casually at the batsman, a teasing grin, a speech bubble near his head showing a tiny scoreboard reading "90" next to a cricket ball with a spin swirl, standing for the semi-final score and the spinner. In the background, two teammates watch from the bench, one smiling knowingly, one with eyebrows raised. On the whiteboard behind them a simple line reads "FINAL". A small coral curved arrow runs from the captain's bubble to the batsman's hands on the pad, showing the words caused the move. Mood: warm team banter, a flicker of challenge, afternoon light through the window. Label: "PADS UP" at the top right of the picture.

key: A school principal needs a teacher
name: ch21_principal_class_10c
alt: A school principal tells an experienced teacher that the difficult 10-C class needs someone special, and the teacher steps up toward the classroom door.
scene: An Indian school corridor seen from the side. LEFT: the door of a classroom with a plaque reading "10-C"; through its window we see a few paper planes in the air and a toppled chair, and beside the door a small board with three teacher name cards crossed out in coral, showing three class teachers have quit. CENTRE: the principal, a woman in her late 50s in a plum saree and spectacles, holding a register to her chest, faces the teacher with a serious but warm expression, one hand open toward the 10-C door. Her speech bubble shows a gold star above a single figure silhouette, standing for someone special. RIGHT: the teacher, a man in his 40s in a light amber shirt with a pen in his pocket and a stack of notebooks under one arm, stands straighter, chin up, one sleeve being rolled up, already taking a step toward the door; a small bubble above him shows a raised hand. Behind the principal a faint dashed outline of a support hand rests on the teacher's shoulder, showing she will back him. Afternoon light from corridor windows on a pale wall with a notice board. Mood: honest, a little daring. Label: "SOMEONE SPECIAL" at the top centre of the picture.

key: A street cricket team plays every evening
name: ch21_street_cricket_dusk
alt: Kids play cricket in a dusty lane at dusk with brick stumps and a shared water bottle, and the batsman hits a six over a neighbour's wall.
scene: A narrow dusty Indian lane at dusk, low orange sun setting at the far end between houses, long shadows, a single street lamp just switched on. LEFT: two bricks stacked as stumps, a wicketkeeper boy of 12 in a striped tee crouching behind them. CENTRE: the batsman, a boy of 14 in a coral tee and shorts, finishes a big swing with a taped tennis-ball bat, eyes following the ball. A dashed arc carries the ball up and over a neighbour's plastered compound wall on the right, where a potted plant and laundry line show it is a home. RIGHT: the bowler, a boy in a teal tee, has his hands on his head in mock despair, and a girl fielder in an amber kurta leaps in celebration. Foreground at the edge of the pitch: a single shared steel water bottle and a few chappals left in a pile, plus a chalk scoreboard scratched on the wall reading "42". At the far end of the lane, two boys from the next lane watch with arms folded, the rivals. No money, no trophies anywhere. Mood: joyful, dusty, golden fading light, kept on a pale ground. Labels: "SIX!" near the top of the ball's arc and "THE GAME ITSELF" across the top of the picture.

key: A mother wants her two children
name: ch21_fridge_chalkboard_race
alt: A small chalkboard on the fridge lists two children and the times they finished homework, and both children race to the table with their books while their mother smiles.
scene: An Indian home kitchen and dining corner in the early evening, a window showing a dusky sky, a tube light on. LEFT: a white fridge with fruit magnets and a small black chalkboard stuck on its door, two rows written in chalk: "RIYA 6:30" and "ARJUN 6:32", and a stick of chalk on a string. Beside the fridge, the mother, a woman in her late 30s in a teal salwar kameez with a dupatta, stirs a steel pot of dal on the stove, glancing over her shoulder with an amused smile. A wall clock shows half past six. RIGHT: a small dining table with two chairs, where a girl of about 10 (coral frock, two plaits) slaps a finished notebook down triumphantly, and a boy of about 8 (amber tee) runs in clutching his schoolbag and books, cheeks puffed, determined to be next. A dashed arrow loops from the chalkboard to the table, showing the board drives the race. On the table, two pencils, an eraser and a geometry box. No scolding stick, no prize, just the times. Mood: playful, lively evening home. Label: "DONE AT" in chalk above the board's two rows, and "RACE TO 6:30" across the top of the picture.

key: Persuading your parents to let you move cities
name: ch21_sunday_lunch_six_months
alt: Over a relaxed Sunday lunch a young man shows his parents office photos on his phone and asks for six months, while his father points to a PG near the uncle's house.
scene: A relaxed Sunday lunch at an Indian family dining table, seen from the side: steel plates with rice, dal, a bowl of curd and papad, a jug of water. LEFT: the father, a man in his late 50s with spectacles and a grey moustache in a plum kurta, leans in with one finger pointing at a small inset bubble showing a little house with the label "PG" next to a bigger house, standing for the PG near the uncle's place, his worried frown softening. CENTRE: the mother, in her early 50s in an amber saree, holds a hand to her cheek, talking, her bubble showing a small phone with a heart, meaning daily calls. RIGHT: the son, about 24, in a teal shirt, sits calmly, palms open, holding out his phone showing a tall office building photo, and a small paper beside his plate marked with a rupee sign for the salary slip. Above him a speech bubble shows a calendar page with "6" and a curved return arrow toward a little house, meaning six months then come back if it fails. A suitcase stands half-hidden behind his chair. A window shows a midday sun. Mood: warm, calm, persuasive, no argument. Label: "GIVE ME SIX MONTHS" across the top centre of the picture.
